note: Post-Apoc's adapter onto the material library (core/materials/PLAN.md). Families are MAT keys (src/22-mat.js), bound in place by src/29y-pa-matlib.js at TILE[key] metres per UV unit (src/20-tex.js), so scale is in metres. Vertex colours carry the livery and the weathering (22-mat.js WEATHER), so the sets go grey (keep 0) at the measured mean of the procedural map they replace (2026-10-06); metalness stays low (no environment map). The corrugate and container walls (corr, cont) take metal.corrugated.rusty (2026-10-06, late: rust streaks kept at 85 % of their own colour; the container's ribs at 3x the scale); the patch sheets and iron (sheet, iron) stay procedural: the library corrugate, container rib, tin patchwork and rust plate came out clean and grey at eye level, and the rust streaks are the set's look (2026-10-06 comparison). steel (no brushed-steel set yet), bottle (glass.bottle is swirled glass, not bottle bases), chain and corrH (horizontal ribs) stay procedural. Run python3 tools/textures/pack.py kits/post-apoc after any change, then python3 build.py; ?mat=proc shows the procedural look.
